newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch firmer but buying limited.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch firmer but buying limited.

text.p: Gold and silver prices firmed slightly from Monday's lows on Tuesday but dealers described the level of follow-though buying as disappointing.
Gold firmed on short covering following a comment from the Japanese prime minister that his government had considered selling from reserves of U.S. treasury bills and buying gold.
Bullion was fixed at $338.65 per ounce, just 65 cents firmer than on Monday afternoon which itself showed some recovery from a fresh low since February 12 of $336.95 set that morning.
"After these comments and the Dow and the dollar coming off, gold's reaction has been disappointing," one dealer said.
The comments caused turmoil in U.S. financial markets late on Monday. A Ministry of Finance official later said they had been misinterpreted.
"U.S. Treasuries are a highly advantageous, secure and essential investment instrument for Japan's foreign currency reserves," the official said.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, responding to a question after a speech at Columbia University, said Japan had in the past been tempted to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities and boost its gold reserves, but had not done so.

"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in co-operation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto added.
But gold dealers focused more on the increasing short position gathering on Comex after a 7,000-lot increase in open interest was posted on Friday.
"There seems to be a big bet by the funds on the downside and that is why gold didn't shoot up," one dealer said.
He added that a few more days of the Dow Jones Industrial Average coming off and the strategy could look vulnerable.
Even so gold was fundamentally bearish and could be limited to range trading between $335/$336 and $342.00 if the downside held, dealers said.
The silver outlook was better after it moved to establish a base at $4.80/$4.82 where it was unchanged on Tuesday.
"Silver could be the one to break out to the top side. If it got past yesterday's top ($4.85) we could see 10 cents more, easily," one dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both slightly easier at $414.00/$418.00 down $5.00 and $194.00/$199.00 down $2.50 respectively.
